title: Rigveda 5.18: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.18: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.18 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 333v-334r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.18.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 333v
translation.original_text:
1prā̱tar a̱gniḥ pu̍rupri̱yo vi̱śaḥ sta̍ve̱tāti̍thiḥ | viśvā̍ni̱ yo ama̍rtyo ha̱vyā marte̍ṣu̱ raṇya̍ti ||
2dvi̱tāya̍ mṛ̱ktavā̍hase̱ svasya̱ dakṣa̍sya ma̱ṁhanā̍ | indu̱ṁ sa dha̍tta ānu̱ṣak sto̱tā ci̍t te amartya ||
translation.text:
1AT dawn let: Agni, much-beloved guest of the house, be glorified; Immortal who delights in all oblations brought by mortal men.
2For Dvita who receives through wealth of native strength maimed offerings, Thy praiser even gains at once the Soma-drops, Immortal Gods!
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 333v (numbered 6v by the scribe) (OPenn image 334, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.17.3 ‹yaḥ ayukta tujā girā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 334r (numbered 7r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.18.3 ‹ariṣṭaḥ yeṣām rathaḥ vi›. Verses 5.18.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1prātaḥ | agniḥ | puru-priyaḥ | viśaḥ | staveta | atithiḥ | viśvāni | yaḥ | amartyaḥ | havyā | marteṣu | raṇyati
2dvitāya | mṛkta-vāhase | svasya | dakṣasya | maṃhanā | indum | saḥ | dhatte | ānuṣak | stotā | cit te | amartya

translation.original_ref: RV 5.18.3-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 334r
translation.original_text:
3taṁ vo̍ dī̱rghāyu̍śociṣaṁ gi̱rā hu̍ve ma̱ghonā̍m | ari̍ṣṭo̱ yeṣā̱ṁ ratho̱ vy a̍śvadāva̱nn īya̍te ||
4ci̱trā vā̱ yeṣu̱ dīdhi̍tir ā̱sann u̱kthā pānti̱ ye | stī̱rṇam ba̱rhiḥ sva̍rṇare̱ śravā̍ṁsi dadhire̱ pari̍ ||
5ye me̍ pañcā̱śata̍ṁ da̱dur aśvā̍nāṁ sa̱dhastu̍ti | dyu̱mad a̍gne̱ mahi̱ śravo̍ bṛ̱hat kṛ̍dhi ma̱ghonā̍ṁ nṛ̱vad a̍mṛta nṛ̱ṇām ||
translation.text:
3Nobles, with song I call that car of yours that shines with lengthened life, For, God who givest steeds! that car hither and thither goes unharmed.
4They who have varied ways of thought, who guard, the lauds within their lips, And strew the grass before the light, have decked themselves with high renown.
5Immortal Agni, give the chiefs, heroes who institute the rite, Heroes' illustrious, lofty fame, who at the synod met for praise presented me with fifty steeds.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 334r (numbered 7r by the scribe) (OPenn image 334, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.18.3 ‹ariṣṭaḥ yeṣām rathaḥ vi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 334v (numbered 7v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.19.4 ‹-priyam dugdham na kāmyam›. Verses 5.18.3-5 end on this page; 5.18.3 begins on fol. 333v (numbered 6v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
3tam | vaḥ | dīrghāyu-śociṣam | girā | huve | maghonām | ariṣṭaḥ | yeṣām | rathaḥ | vi | aśva-dāvan | īyate
4citrā | vā | yeṣu | dīdhitiḥ | āsan | ukthā | pānti | ye | stīrṇam | barhiḥ | svaḥ-nare | śravāṃsi | dadhire | pari
5ye | me | pañcāśatam | daduḥ | aśvānām | sadha-stuti | dyu-mat | agne | mahi | śravaḥ | bṛhat | kṛdhi | maghonām | nṛ-vat | amṛta | nṛṇām
